2609.17953.title: EDCT-Bench: Uncovering Faithfulness Gaps in VLMs via Explanation-Driven Counterfactual Testing
2609.17953.paper_summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) can produce Natural Language Explanations (NLEs) that sound plausible yet remain inconsistent with the visual evidence they cite. We present Explanation-Driven Counterfactual Testing (EDCT), an intervention-based protocol that extracts visual concepts cited in a model's explanation, applies verified minimal edits to them, and tests whether the resulting answer and explanation remain consistent with the edited image. Using this protocol, we create EDCT-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark spanning three complementary domains: knowledge-intensive visual question answering (OK-VQA), safety-critical driving (DriveLM), and 3D spatial reasoning (3DSRBench). Across the evaluated VLMs, EDCT reveals substantial faithfulness gaps, with models frequently producing responses inconsistent with verified visual changes. Finally, our fine-tuning study suggests that EDCT-generated counterfactuals provide high-impact training signals.
2609.17953.paper_summary_zh: 視覺-語言模型（VLMs）可以產生聽起來合理但與其引用的視覺證據不一致的自然語言解釋（NLEs）。我們提出了解釋驅動的反事實測試（EDCT），這是一種基於干預的協議，提取模型解釋中引用的視覺概念，對其進行經過驗證的最小編輯，並測試結果的答案和解釋是否與編輯後的圖像保持一致。使用這一協議，我們創建了EDCT-Bench，這是一個涵蓋三個互補領域的綜合基準：知識密集型視覺問題回答（OK-VQA）、安全關鍵駕駛（DriveLM）和三維空間推理（3DSRBench）。在評估的VLMs中，EDCT揭示了顯著的忠實度差距，模型經常產生與經過驗證的視覺變化不一致的回應。最後，我們的微調研究表明，EDCT生成的反事實提供了高影響力的訓練信號。
